newsitem.title: ESTONIA: IMF AND ESTONIA START PRELIMINARY TALKS.
newsitem.headline: IMF AND ESTONIA START PRELIMINARY TALKS.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund and the Estonian governement have started preliminary negotiations for a new stand-by arrangment, the IMF said on Thursday.

"The current stand-by arrangement is to expire in summer and we have started preliminary talks to set the base for discussions to be held in August," Dimitri Demekas, the IMF's resident representative to Estonia told Reuters.
A full IMF mission will arrive in Estonia in August to negotiate the next stand-by arrangement.
"The government said in its programme that it wants a new arrangement and we need to know what their plans are in both macro and fiscal policy as well as in structural reforms," Demekas added.
The IMF is also interested in the government's response to the rising current account deficit.
"One of the major issues is also the existing current account deficit and what sort of fiscal policy is needed to be taken to deal with it," Demekas added.
